subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: For spawned subagent runs that lose the selected Codex/OpenAI OAuth route, should OpenClaw fail closed, visibly warn and continue fallback, or keep log-only fallback after OAuth inheritance is proven?
rationale: The choice controls whether private scheduled/channel context may cross provider boundaries after an auth failure, and repo policy treats auth/provider routing and fallback behavior as compatibility- and security-sensitive.

options.title: Require live proof and visible/fail-closed behavior
options.body: Keep this open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and implement either fail-closed behavior or an operator-visible warning for auth-route loss.

options.title: Split fallback visibility after propagation proof
options.body: Close only the OAuth propagation portion after live proof and track fallback visibility or fail-closed policy in a narrower canonical issue.

options.title: Accept log-only fallback
options.body: Treat source-level OAuth inheritance as sufficient after proof and accept the privacy and operator-surprise tradeoff of existing fallback logging.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and visible/fail-closed behavior
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and implement either fail-closed behavior or an operator-visible warning for auth-route loss.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review history ties steipete to the cross-surface provider/auth/session routing area, making them the best available owner for the policy choice even though Ayaan Zaidi owns the newest line-level fix history.
